result.title: Distributed Subliminal Learning: Replacing Model Updates with Random-Carrier Outputs
result.comment: Accepted to the Collaborative, Open, and DECentralized training of Foundation Models workshop at NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: Collaborative learning typically exchanges model parameters: federated clients communicate updates, while independently adapted foundation models are combined by exchanging adapters or checkpoints. This makes communication scale with model size and requires local specializations to be reconciled in weight space, where interference is common. We ask whether knowledge can instead be shared through model behavior on task-unrelated inputs. We introduce Distributed Subliminal Learning (DSL), a collaborative learning primitive in which participants adapt a common model locally, probe it with task-unrelated inputs, and transmit only the resulting carrier outputs. A coordinator pools these outputs and distills them into a shared model. The primitive supports one-shot foundation-model composition through carrier completions and iterative federated learning through carrier logits, without transmitting model updates or requiring task-related proxy data. In LLM composition, compared with LoRA averaging, DSL achieves higher preference retention (94.56% vs. 87.76%) and a larger GSM8K gain over the base model (22.0 vs. 0.6 points), while reducing upload by 30.6-49.0$\times$. In federated classification, DSL reaches 96.83% on MNIST with 8.9$\times$ less uplink than FedAvg and provides lower-communication operating points on CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet. These results establish random-carrier outputs as a practical communication primitive for knowledge sharing across distinct collaborative learning paradigms.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出分布式潜意识学习（DSL）：参与者本地适配共享模型后，用与任务无关的输入探测模型，仅传输其输出（carrier completions 或 logits），由协调方汇总并蒸馏回共享模型，从而在不上传参数的情况下实现知识共享。
AI.relevance_reason: 以行为输出而非权重作为知识载体，可供核查 LVR 中「信息是否真正编码在内部状态并被答案使用」的旁路与坍缩问题；其潜意识信道是否传递了任务必要视觉信息、以及可迁移到 latent 状态更新的监督与贡献分配设计，尚需读原文验证。
